pr_body:
Occasionally, it's useful to be able to use non-printable,
RTL (right-to-left) or other non-standard unicode characters
in an EQL query.

Introducing the standard `\uXXXX` escape sequence as well as
the variable 2-8 char escape sequence `\u{XXXXXXXX}`, e.g.:

```
\u0023
\u{35}
\u{1f2da}
\u{002acd1}
```

Closes: #62832
pr_title: EQL: Allow Unicode escape sequences in strings
pr_comment:
- Chose not add in the grammar the support for the new unicode escape sequences for the old style string quoting as for those kind of strings the user will get and error anyway.

- I'm still undecided to if we should go with the current approach where the grammar rules are responsible for a big portion of the tokens allowed, or if we should simply add the `\u` in the grammar and then treat everything else in the `AbstractBuilder`. The latter has a simpler grammar, a bit more complex java code, but imho better error messages. e.g.: We could have a regex pattern for the hex digits and report `Non hex-digit characters found ....`
As discussed, removed support for `\u1234` and only allow the `\u{...}`.
